newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sorry Europe not invited to Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: France sorry Europe not invited to Mideast talks.

text.p: France said a Middle East summit announced by Washington on Sunday could be useful in the search for peace but regretted that no European leaders had been invited to attend.

"If the situation can pass from crisis to negotiations, this is positive...and from this point of view, this meeting in Washington can be useful," French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on RTL television.

Asked how France and other European powers could contribute as they had not been invited to Washington, de Charette said: "That is certainly unfortunate. That is certainly not a positive step for things to go forward."

France, long interested in a higher profile in Middle East diplomacy, had repeatedly offered to play a central role in the search for common ground between Israel and the Palestinians after violence last week in which nearly 70 people were killed.

But it was U.S. President Bill Clinton who announced that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, King Hussein of Jordan and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak had been invited to meet in Washington.
